title: Creating a Flag to Remember

steps.label: Step 1
steps.title: Name Donors
paragraphs: Name Donors submit the name of a fallen Service Member or First Responder to be sewn onto our flags at no cost. Regardless of the cause of death, in or after their service, they are honored on a flag.
Donors choose the uniform pattern that best represents their loved one’s service.
All registered names are added to our database and placed indefinitely in a queue for inclusion on future flags.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.title: Flag Hosts
paragraphs: Flag Hosts are businesses and organizations dedicated to publicly displaying our flags in the spotlight of our communities, as lasting tributes to our heroes. These flags provide comfort to grieving families and unite communities; strengthening a grateful nation to the sacrifices made.
Becoming a Flag Host means gaining nationwide visibility while redefining remembrance.

Each flag goes through four meticulous stages: Printing, sewing, framing (if needed), and final dedication. A one-time donation covers the labor and materials, keeping our flags flying high across the country.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.title: Building the Flag
paragraphs: Our flags have unique features that make them profoundly symbolic and impactful.

features.title: The Union
features.text: The blue portion of the flag represents the “Union” and is printed with Military and First Responder insignia. Encircling them are 21 stars, symbolizing the traditional 21-gun salute. Our Foundation’s logo is printed on the back of the flag.

features.title: Name Tape
features.text: Each fallen hero’s name is sewn onto the flag using an actual uniform name tape from their service. Name Donors can personalize it with nicknames, dates, or a standard rank and name.

features.title: Serial Number
features.text: Every flag has a unique serial number, allowing Name Donors to track the flag’s journey. Visitors can post and tag the flag’s picture and number on social media, promoting awareness and remembrance.

steps.label: Step 4
steps.title: Flag Dedication
paragraphs: Flag Hosts often invite the community to unveil the flag and discuss the importance of its display. Families of the flag receive a newsletter email inviting them to see their newest flag be revealed. Once dedicated, we notify all families with details about the Flag Host, to include pictures.
When available, Anthony Peterson, the founder will travel to attend a dedication and speak to the families, if requested.

pricing.title: Donation Costs & Flag Sizes
pricing.lede: 10% of every flag goes toward donating a framed flag to an organization in need.
pricing.text: Every Flag to Remember is built by hand with the same care as our very first flag. Your donation covers materials, labor, and shipping, plus framing for the Framed Flag.

sizes.name: Framed Flag
sizes.text: Includes Flag to Remember coins and a dedication plate with the flag’s theme, number, dedication date, and Flag Host. Ships in a heavy-duty protective case so it arrives safely.
